The contest census primitive establishes a foundational kernel for DFS strategy by enumerating all active contests and categorizing them by game type. This enables GSE to compute field size expectations and optimize for variance in entry fees and prize pools. The ownership projection primitive then applies Bayesian inference to estimate player participation probabilities, which informs chalk vs. contrarian decisions. The payout structure point primitive maps these elements into a risk-return vector space, enabling GSE to select lineups that maximize utility under uncertainty. These primitives form a dual framework where contest enumeration drives strategic scope, while ownership and payout data refine tactical execution. Failure modes include overfitting to historical data or misalignment between projected and actual contest dynamics.
